set.body:
EVIDENCE THAT CUTS AGAINST THE USABILITY THESIS. I executed the full README path under pkgload::load_all() and inspected what a user actually sees. Recording this because the rest of this workstream is critical and the criticism should not be allowed to imply things that are false.

WHAT THE USER SEES IS GOOD. Verbatim:

  <effect_contrast_view>
    measurements: 6
   measurement     signed   coherent configuration    total coherence_fraction
      feature1  0.9250000 0.85000000     1.2500000 2.100000        0.404761905
      feature2  0.1333333 0.01666667     2.0833333 2.100000        0.007936508

  <effect_rdm_view>
    measurements: 6
   measurement face - house face - object house - object
      feature1     2.100000      1.400000      0.2250000

The RDM view labels its columns 'face - house', 'face - object', 'house - object'. That is
domain vocabulary, not framework vocabulary, and it is immediately readable by anyone who
has done RSA. coherence_fraction is computed and displayed without being asked for. These
print methods are better than most packages in this space.

BETTER STILL, print(plan):

  <effect_geometry_plan>
    lowering:     additive_contraction
    dense payload: 864 bytes
    state:        query-first; call geometry(plan) to materialize

That last line TEACHES the plan/materialize distinction at the console, at the moment the
user holds the object, and tells them the exact next call. This is the Class II distinction
from bd-01KZY8X53W0DQ8P99AD0V0CF7F being taught rather than renamed - which is precisely the
remedy that bead prescribes. It is already implemented. It just is not carried into the prose.

SO THE DIAGNOSIS SHARPENS. The package is not uniformly inaccessible. Measured honestly:

  approach path   costly    7 statements / 9 calls before the first interpretable number,
                            starting from effect matrices the user must already possess
  result layer    good      readable, domain-labelled, self-teaching

Comparative: rMVPA reaches an equivalent result in 5 calls after library(), and those 5
INCLUDE generating the data. effectagram needs 7 statements with the data already in hand.
The true gap is therefore wider than 7-versus-5, because the two counts do not start from
the same place.

CONSEQUENCE FOR REMEDIATION - this is the useful part. The fix is not to redesign the result
layer and not to soften vocabulary at the end of the pipeline. It is to shorten and re-narrate
the approach. Specifically the three objects a user must construct before anything happens -
effect_space(), abstract_domain(), relation() - are all pure declaration, and a generator plus
a documented example would let a reader see a result FIRST and learn those three objects
afterward, when they have a reason to care.

One correction to my own earlier claim on bd-01KZY8MT8WGDG8R8J3JQ5KKKC0. I wrote there that
print.effect_geometry:128 reporting 'signed cross-generalized form; PSD not assumed' was
machinery vocabulary where a user wants shape information. Having now seen it in context, the
line above it already reports 'effects: 3 x 3' and 'measurements: 6', so the shape IS there and
the PSD line is an additional honest warning rather than a substitute for shape. That specific
criticism was wrong and I withdraw it. The framing criticism in that bead stands; this one line
does not support it.
set.title: Verified: the result layer is already accessible; the cost is entirely in the approach path
